title: Generator Maintenance Log
subtitle: Standby Generator Maintenance: preserves changes and next triggers.
description: Generator Maintenance Log covers engine-generator, transfer equipment, fuel system, starting system, and load served. The facility emergency-power coordinator records Standby Generator Maintenance events, owners, exceptions, and next triggers. Generator Maintenance Log keeps Standby Generator Maintenance exceptions visible until the facility emergency-power coordinator handoff.
use_case: Use Generator Maintenance Log at generator enclosure, fuel area, transfer switch, and served distribution. Document engine-generator, transfer equipment, fuel system, starting system, and load served identity before Standby Generator Maintenance begins. Compare engine-generator, transfer equipment, fuel system, starting system, and load served findings with stated Standby Generator Maintenance criteria; route unresolved Standby Generator Maintenance issues to qualified generator service supervisor. For Generator Maintenance Log, confirm requirements for Standby Generator Maintenance. Ask qualified generator service supervisor to review Standby Generator Maintenance conditions beyond the facility emergency-power coordinator's role.

sections.title: Tracking period and subject identity
sections.guidance: For Standby Generator Maintenance, identify responsible parties, generator enclosure, fuel area, transfer switch, and served distribution, and the linked engine-generator, transfer equipment, fuel system, starting system, and load served source.

fields.label: Make, model, serial, rating, and fuel type
Maintenance interval, hour meter, and last-load-test reference

sections.title: Status events and next-control history
sections.guidance: Capture Standby Generator Maintenance facts for engine-generator, transfer equipment, fuel system, starting system, and load served; include result, limit, source, and next control.

blocks.label: Standby Generator Maintenance tracked controls
items: Fluid levels, leaks, hoses, belts, and exhaust condition
Battery, charger, terminals, and starting result
Fuel supply, containment, and visible piping condition
Cooling, ventilation, louvers, and enclosure condition
No-load or authorized load operating readings
Transfer, alarms, shutdowns, and return-to-normal result

sections.title: Current status outcome and next update
sections.guidance: For Standby Generator Maintenance, preserve each open variance with its current state, accountable owner, and next dated update. Facility Emergency-Power Coordinator performs period review.

blocks.label: Status exceptions, overdue actions, and retained evidence
items: Abnormal temperature, pressure, vibration, or noise
Failed start, transfer, alarm, or shutdown
Load test requested without safe approved conditions
Oil, coolant, voltage, frequency, and pressure readings
blocks.guidance: Pause Standby Generator Maintenance when fuel, exhaust, electrical, starting, transfer, or shutdown concern prevents safe standby readiness. Retain the available Standby Generator Maintenance proof and route unresolved engine-generator, transfer equipment, fuel system, starting system, and load served scope to facility emergency-power coordinator.
